top.line: An answer to Nitin Pandya: kill switches stop models, not valid workflows acting on tampered records.
top.para: Sign the change, check it outside.

in-short.line: A tampered record and a valid workflow; sign every change that can move money; check it outside.

question.line: Nitin Pandya asks who answers to the regulator when an agent releases money on a tampered record.
question.para: The CISO, the model owner or operations?

advisories.line: CERT-In and I4C advisories: disbursal APIs, mule accounts, Rs 65 crore from 12 NBFCs in one case.
advisories.para: As reported by Cyble, MediaNama and The Federal.

gap.line: The RBI draft asks for kill switches; the failure here is a record changed without proof of authority.

control.line: Each change carries a signed mandate; a verifier outside the workflow checks it; no mandate, no money.

ours.line: Our own incident: a commit signed by an unregistered key went live; now a signer check refuses it.
ours.para: Nothing refused it. Only Dinis noticed.

accountability.line: The key that signed the change, the grantor of that key, and the owner of the policy that accepted it.

limits.line: Advisories read through reporting; some claims only in the post; stolen keys; our case is code.

sources.line: The post, reporting on the advisories, the RBI draft, our incident note and decisions site.
